title: Los cinco sonidos y el acento
summary: The five pure Spanish vowels and where the stress falls — plus the tilde

blocks.title: Five vowels, always the same
blocks.body: Spanish has **five pure vowels** and each one has **exactly one sound**, every single time. No silent letters, no drift. Say them short and clean: **a** as in *casa*, **e** as in *mesa*, **i** as in *sí*, **o** as in *sol*, **u** as in *luna*.

blocks.title: Tap to hear the five vowels
Where's the stress?
blocks.body: Every Spanish word has one **stressed syllable** (*sílaba tónica*). The default rule: words ending in a **vowel, -n or -s** stress the **second-to-last** syllable (*ca-**sa**, ta-**pas**). Words ending in any other consonant stress the **last** (*ho-**tel**, ciu-**dad**).
blocks.callout: Stress matters: *papa* (potato) vs *papá* (dad) are different words.

blocks.title: The tilde marks the exceptions
blocks.body: When a word breaks the default rule, a written accent — the **tilde** — shows the real stress: *ca-**fé***, *mú-si-ca*, *A-**mé**-ri-ca*. The tilde is **not decoration** — it tells you where to push, and sometimes changes the meaning entirely.
blocks.callout: *está* (is) vs *esta* (this): same letters, the accent is the whole difference.

blocks.explain: *gracias* ends in -s, so the default rule puts the stress on the second-to-last syllable: **GRA**-cias. No tilde needed.
